name: Globe Guesser
author: kairos
description: Guess where in the world a photo was taken. Five rounds, an OpenStreetMap map and a spinnable globe to click, and photographs of real places from Wikipedia. Falls back to a bundled offline map when there is no network.

barWidget.description: Guess where a photo was taken, on an OpenStreetMap map or a globe

schema.label: Difficulty
schema.description: Which cities a round can be drawn from. Easy uses the 150 largest in the world, normal the largest 500, hard all 1000 - including places you have very likely never heard of.

schema.label: Rounds per game
schema.description: How many photos make up one game. Five is the classic run, worth 25,000 points.

schema.label: Starting view
schema.description: Whether a round opens on the flat world map or the globe. You can switch at any time during a round; this only sets which one you start on.

schema.label: Photo radius (km)
schema.description: How far from a city centre a place may be. 10 km is both the default and MediaWiki's hard ceiling for a geosearch, so this only ever narrows the search. Smaller keeps photos in the city centre; it also finds fewer of them.

schema.label: CARTO basemap key (optional)
schema.description: Optional. Leave empty and the map is drawn from bundled offline outlines, which needs no key and no account. CARTO began watermarking unauthenticated map tiles in August 2026, so detailed street-level tiles now need a key of your own: get a free one at carto.com/basemaps/apikey (5 million tiles a month). The key is used only to fetch map tiles.
